subject: Unexpected collection attempt & overage breakdown request - OrbitAI
messages:
From: Laura Kim <laura.kim@orbitai.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Finance Ops <fin-ops@orbitai.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 13:12:00 -0500
Subject: Unexpected collection attempt and a surprising overage on Dec invoice

Hi Ben,

We saw an attempted collection against our account this morning for the December invoice and noticed a ~27% overage line labelled 'ingest-burst-202612' that we don't recognize. We never ran a bulk ingest job in that window and our engineering team can't find any scheduled jobs.

Can you please:
- Share the per-session logs (timestamps + request ids) that led to the overage calculation for Dec 1-3
- Confirm whether this collection attempt was escalated or automatic (we got both an invoice and a collection notification)
- Clarify if EU VAT was applied to that overage (we are a US entity but our staging runs in eu-central occasionally)

I attached the invoice notice we received (invoice_202612.pdf). We need to decide whether to pause payment while you investigate — please treat this as urgent.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Kim
Head of Finance, OrbitAI
laura.kim@orbitai.com
+1 415 555 0142

Attachments: invoice_202612.pdf

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Kim <laura.kim@orbitai.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Unexpected collection attempt and a surprising overage on Dec invoice

Hi Laura — thanks for flagging this and for the invoice. I'm pausing the collection hold in our billing system while we look into the logs; you should not be automatically charged while we investigate (I'll confirm in writing once the hold is set).

Initial notes: our telemetry indicates a sudden series of parallel sessions from one API key between 2026-12-01T03:02:12Z and 2026-12-01T03:15:08Z that drove token counts up. That could be a replay / duplicate-submission event. I've asked our usage team to produce a per-request export and session samples — attaching them when ready.

Next steps from our side:
- Marissa (billing) will produce a CSV extract with per-request timestamps and request_ids for Dec 1-3.
- Rishi (customer success / account owner) will coordinate with you on whether to offer a one-time pro-rated credit if this was accidental.
- We will confirm VAT treatment once we know the tenant-region tagging for those sessions.

I'll follow up by EOD with the initial extract.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: (none on this message)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 15:28:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Unexpected collection attempt and a surprising overage on Dec invoice

Ben / Rishi — attaching the export you asked for. The CSV includes token_count, request_id, api_key_id, region_tag, and session_id for the window 2026-12-01 to 2026-12-03. I also pulled three full session samples (session-sample-20261206.json) that show identical payloads replayed across multiple request_ids.

Preliminary observations:
- api_key_id: ak_live_78d9 shows ~18x parallel requests between 03:02 and 03:05 UTC.
- region_tag values are mixed: two-thirds marked as us-central, one-third as eu-central.
- The suspect sessions have identical prompt text lengths and identical streaming patterns — looks like a replay or client-side retry loop rather than distinct user traffic.

I recommend the following:
1) Offer a goodwill credit for the duplicate traffic (suggested amount: credit equal to the calculated duplicate tokens for that window)
2) Reissue an updated invoice removing the duplicate lines and mark the original invoice as under review to prevent collection repeat
3) If Orbit requests, provide the session samples and CSV for their audit team (redact PII if present)

I can prepare a redline of the invoice and a one-time credit authorization if you approve.

Attachments: usage_export_202612.csv, session-sample-20261206.json

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Unexpected collection attempt and a surprising overage on Dec invoice

Thanks Marissa — good catch. Ben, I spoke with Orbit briefly this morning: they're worried about cashflow timing through month-end. From a customer success perspective I'd rather avoid forcing a collections reversal if it's an obvious duplicate issue. Offer a credit and an updated invoice.

We should also confirm EU VAT: because one-third of those sessions are tagged eu-central, accounting wants to know whether VAT was applied on the overage line and if we need to reverse VAT on the credit. I'll loop in Soojin for tax guidance; Soojin, can you confirm whether we should issue a VAT-inclusive credit note or a VAT-adjusted credit?

If Soojin recommends VAT reversal, we should route the credit through our EU billing entity and issue a credit note (not a refund) so Orbit can apply it against the December statement.

Action items:
- Marissa: prepare proposed credit amount and draft updated invoice (I'd like a line showing 'duplicate request credit').
- Ben: confirm with Orbit whether they want the hosted session samples for internal audit.
- Soojin: tax guidance on VAT handling.

—Rishi

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected collection attempt and a surprising overage on Dec invoice

Rishi / team — quick tax note: if the original invoice included VAT on those specific line items (i.e., the taxable supply was treated as supplied in the EU), then our credit needs to mirror the tax treatment. In practice:
- If VAT was charged, the credit note should show the VAT amount reversed and be issued from the same EU entity that issued the invoice.
- If the invoice was net of VAT (US entity), then the credit can be issued without VAT adjustment.

Marissa: can you confirm the billing entity used for the Dec invoice (we have two: Redwood US LLC and Redwood EU Ltd.) and whether VAT appeared on the overage line? I can coordinate with accounting to ensure the credit note has the correct VAT fields.

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Tax & Compliance, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Kim <laura.kim@orbitai.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected collection attempt and a surprising overage on Dec invoice

Hi Laura — quick update and next steps after our internal review.

Summary:
- We identified a set of duplicate/replayed requests tied to api_key ak_live_78d9 that generated the overage. The attached CSV and three session samples show identical payloads across multiple request_ids. (Attached earlier: usage_export_202612.csv, session-sample-20261206.json.)
- We have placed the invoice on hold and halted the collection attempt. You will not be charged while we finalize corrections.
- VAT note: the invoice was issued by Redwood EU Ltd for the overage lines (those sessions were partially tagged eu-central). Soojin will issue a VAT-adjusted credit note from the EU entity.

Proposed remediation:
1) One-time credit equal to the duplicate token charge (we calculated $3,420.00) — this will be applied as a credit note to your Dec statement.
2) Reissued invoice (invoice_202612_revised.pdf) removing the duplicate line and showing the credit note reference CN-2026-ORB-09.
3) We will provide the three session samples and CSV for your audit; we can redact any PII on request.

Please confirm if Orbit wants the raw session samples for your internal audit team. If not, we'll send the CSV + redacted samples. Once you confirm, Marissa will trigger the credit note and accounting will post the adjustment (and we'll share the updated invoice and credit note PDFs and HubSpot deal update).

Apologies for the disruption — we're also adding a safeguard rule on replay patterns to alert earlier.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
